“N0, all” Identification key for packaging system containing one or more element.
"Cat A", "Cat B, "Cat C", "Cat D", "Cat E", "Cat F", "Cat G","Cat H" : Categories specific to the types of packaging defined in the PACK_AGB report (e.g case of packaging for cheese).
For more information, please refer to the methodological report  : Colombin, M., Audoye, P., Farrant, L., Allain, D., Anneraud, C., Bosque, F., Besnier, A., Bozec, A.(2024). Rapport méthodologique : volet emballages Agribalyse 3.2.

The inventory refers to a plastic tray and the associated elements allowing to condition a total weight of 200 g of uncured cheese. This specific tray is made for uncured cheese (for refrigerated conservation).
This inventory of packaging solution can only be used for products in sub-category "Uncured cheeses and similar" (PACK_AGB) : refer to the report for more details. 

The packaging solution describes a plastic tray closed with a plastic lid and plastic upper lid.
The data was produced from study of packaging on the French market (supermarket reference) and data collection from manufacturers. 
The inventory includes : (1) production of packaging materials***, (2) manufacture and finishing of packaging components, (3) intermediate transport from the production of materials to the packaging site, and (4) the end-of-life management of packaging*** as it takes place in France. ***Application of CCF, rate of virgin and recycled materials corresponding to the FR scenario (2022) 
The inventory does not include distribution transport (integrated into the next stage “at distribution” in AGRIBALYSE)

The packaging solutions developed as part of the PACK_AGB project have not been developed for use in comparative LCAs of packaging solutions: if this is your purpose, we recommend that you follow the ADEME reference framework on comparative comparative LCA between different packaging solutions: https://librairie.ademe.fr/dechets-economie-circulaire/5309-cadre-de-reference-acv-comparatives-entre-differentes-solutions-d-emballages.html

Assumptions at each stage: 

Production
- Only the packaging material in contact with the product or ensuring the product's shelf life is modeled.
For example, in the case of cookies packaged in PP plastic bags (element 1), themselves packaged in a cardboard box (elements 2): (i) Element 2 is the heaviest / (ii) Element 1 is in contact with the product, so the PP material was taken into account.
- For multi-element and multi-layer packaging, the inventory calls for the material in contact with the product and for the quantity, an assumption has been made to take of the packaging solution (sum of all elements) and consider this value for this material.

Processing
- Only the most representative process for the most representative packaging material is included.

- Datasets created as part of the PACK AGB project were used for the most representative process.

comment:
AGRIBALYSE v3.2 dataset, 2024.
original ecoinvent name: Vanilla {MG}| vanilla production | Cut-off, U

This dataset has been adapted for Agribalyse to represent Vanilla production in Madagascar (recommandations from CIRAD, 2022).
- no mecanisation
- lower Yield_ 
- no land use change
- negative metal emissions have been set to 0
_________________

This dataset represents the production of 1 kg of vanilla. The average Yield_ from 2013 is 750 kg/ha. The data are representative for vanilla production in Madagascar used for the export market. No mineral NPK fertiliser are applied. No organic fertilisers are applied. No pesticides are applied.

The dataset was modelled within the project 'World Food LCA database (WFLDB)'. The aim of this project was to provide inventories of a broad variety of agricultural products and processes and to cover for each product at least 50% of the global export market. The export share of vanilla produced in the Madagascar could not be assessed within this project. The production system regarded in this dataset aimed at representing vanilla produced in the Madagascar for the export market.

PEF-Quality: data quality rating (DQR) = 2.7 (i.e. good quality). This dataset refers to an average situation; for specific situations exchanges might differ substantially due to site specific parameters

Production volume: 2888000 kg
Included activities start: This activity starts with the nursery of vanilla plants.
Included activities end: This activity ends with the harvest of vanilla at farm gate. The dataset includes all activities of a year in the productive phase (8 years) and transport on farm. Activities in the establishment phase (3 years) include manual planting. Activities in the productive phase include harvest of vanilla plants. Further, direct field emissions and land use change are included. Heavy metal uptake by the crop is considered. The dataset doesn't include a) irrigation, fertilisers or pesticides, because they are not applied due to extensive production where cultivation is done mainly manually b) materials for the planting, establishment and clearing phase, and c) drying because vanilla is dried at ambient temperature. Direct field emissions in this prodcution system are not caused by fertilizer or pesticide inputs from humjan activity but are related to deposition of nutrients, nutrient content of the soil and erosion.
Energy values: Undefined
Geography: The inventory is modelled for Madagascar
Technology level: Current
Technology: Conventional production
Start date: 01/01/2013
End date: 31/12/2022
Is data valid for entire period: True
Time period: 
Macro-economic scenario name: Business-as-Usual

comment:
AGRIBALYSE v3.2 dataset, 2024.

The inventory includes : (1) only the main packaging material (in contact with the product) ; (2) the transport for packaging supply (ratio FR and ratio RER) ; (3) only the main process ; (4) the end of life of the main packaging material.

Functional unit: 1kg of packaged food product

The packaging solutions mentioned as “PROXY PACK” have been developed with a simplified approach but are based on datasets from PACK-AGB project. These datasets have not been developed for use in comparative LCAs of packaging solutions: if this is your purpose, we recommend that you follow the ADEME reference framework on comparative comparative LCA between different packaging solutions: https://librairie.ademe.fr/dechets-economie-circulaire/5309-cadre-de-reference-acv-comparatives-entre-differentes-solutions-d-emballages.html

Overall data quality : DQR= 1,75; Technological representativeness (TeR) = 2; Geographical representativeness (GR) = 2; Time-related representativeness (TiR) = 2; Precision (P material) = 1; Precision (P processing) = 1

Time period: Inventory data based on 2023 " Plein Pot Sur les Emballages " (PPSE) data (data from ADEME and Open Food Facts)

Use of "PPSE" data to improve packaging modelling for products not covered by the "PACK AGB" project. Data verified by CTCPA's packaging expert.

General assumptions

For "PPSE" missing data, assumptions are based on CTCPA expertise 
Some multi-layer packaging (identified by CTCPA's expert) are modeled using a packaging solution from PACK AGB project. Nota bene the packaging format may be different.

Assumptions at each stage: 

Production
- Only the packaging material in contact with the product or ensuring the product's shelf life is modeled.
For example, in the case of cookies packaged in PP plastic bags (element 1), themselves packaged in a cardboard box (elements 2): (i) Element 2 is the heaviest / (ii) Element 1 is in contact with the product, so the PP material was taken into account.
- For multi-element and multi-layer packaging, the inventory calls for the material in contact with the product and for the quantity, an assumption has been made to take of the packaging solution (sum of all elements) and consider this value for this material.
- Datasets created as part of the PACK AGB project were used, for the most representative material.

Processing
- Only the most representative process for the most representative packaging material is included.
For example, in the case of a multi-layer flexible film, only the extrusion process is modeled. The lamination process used to combine the various packaging layers was not included. 
- Datasets created as part of the PACK AGB project were used for the most representative process.

Transport
- The assumptions of the PACK AGB project were applied
- Datasets created as part of the PACK AGB project were used, for the most representative packaging material
- Ratios from France and Europe compiled in the PACK AGB project by packaging material were used (ADEME data, 2020).

End of life
- All plastic packaging is considered non-recycled (R2=0%).
To be able to affirm that the plastic packaging is recycled, it is necessary to consider the whole packaging solution (with all the elements and materials) and in this project the dataset only include a part of the packaging (proxy)
- Datasets created as part of the PACK AGB project were used, for the most representative packaging material. 
- The Circular FootPrint Formula was applied.

Included processes: The inventory includes : (1) the processes of soil cultivation, sowing, weed control, fertilisation, pest and pathogen control, harvest; (2) the machines and shed or surface used to park them; (3) all inputs as seed, fertilizers (mineral and organic), active substances, water for irrigation, fuels as well as the transport to the farm; (4) the direct emissions of the fuel combustion, the abrasion of tyres and the direct emissions on the field.
The temporal border of the inventory is 'harvest to harvest'. Fertilizers (K, P and organic N) have been adjusted in order to account for the whole rotation.
Cut-off rule, exclusion : The inventory does not include processes occuring after harvest as 'drying', 'sorting' or 'storing', even if they happen on farm.
Remark: Functional unit:1 kg of fresh matter of ware potato (firm flesh varieties), 80% moisture, conventional production.

Methodological appropriateness and consistency (M) = 1 (very good): >=95%

activityName: Warm sauces chilled, 150g | Packaging System, N0, All, Plastic pot {FR} U
comment:
AGRIBALYSE v3.2 dataset, 2024.

“N0, all” Identification key for packaging system containing one or more element.
For more information, please refer to the methodological report  : Colombin, M., Audoye, P., Farrant, L., Allain, D., Anneraud, C., Bosque, F., Besnier, A., Bozec, A.(2024). Rapport méthodologique : volet emballages Agribalyse 3.2.

The inventory refers to a plastic pot with plastic lids and the associated elements allowing to condition a total weight of 150 g (format) of warm sauces chilled.  
This inventory of packaging solution can only be used for products in sub-category "Warm sauces chilled" (PACK_AGB) : refer to the report for more details. This inventory cannot be used to represent the same type of packaging for other products outside the sub-category "Warm sauces chilled" (PACK_AGB) 

The data was produced from study of packaging on the French market (supermarket reference), weighing and CTCPA packaging expertise.
The inventory includes : (1) production of packaging materials***, (2) manufacture and finishing of packaging components, (3) intermediate transport from the production of materials to the packaging site, and (4) the end-of-life management of packaging*** as it takes place in France. ***Application of CCF, rate of virgin and recycled materials corresponding to the FR scenario (2022) 
The inventory does not include distribution transport (integrated into the next stage “at distribution” in AGRIBALYSE)

The packaging solutions developed as part of the PACK_AGB project have not been developed for use in comparative LCAs of packaging solutions: if this is your purpose, we recommend that you follow the ADEME reference framework on comparative comparative LCA between different packaging solutions: https://librairie.ademe.fr/dechets-economie-circulaire/5309-cadre-de-reference-acv-comparatives-entre-differentes-solutions-d-emballages.html 

Overall data quality : DQR= 2; Technological representativeness (TeR) = 1; Geographical representativeness (GR) = 2; Time-related representativeness (TiR) = 4; Precision (P material) = 1; Precision (P processing) = 1
Time period: the data describing the packaging solution was collected over the period 2020-2022. 
The inventory is modelled for France. Packaging waste management is representative of packaging waste management in France.

activityName: Water, 3000g | Packaging System, Proxy Pack, Plastic bottles {FR} U
comment:
AGRIBALYSE v3.2 dataset, 2024.

The inventory includes : (1) only the main packaging material (in contact with the product) ; (2) the transport for packaging supply (ratio FR and ratio RER) ; (3) only the main process ; (4) the end of life of the main packaging material.

Functional unit: 1kg of packaged food product

The packaging solutions mentioned as “PROXY PACK” have been developed with a simplified approach but are based on datasets from PACK-AGB project. These datasets have not been developed for use in comparative LCAs of packaging solutions: if this is your purpose, we recommend that you follow the ADEME reference framework on comparative comparative LCA between different packaging solutions: https://librairie.ademe.fr/dechets-economie-circulaire/5309-cadre-de-reference-acv-comparatives-entre-differentes-solutions-d-emballages.html

Overall data quality : DQR= 1,25; Technological representativeness (TeR) = 1; Geographical representativeness (GR) = 2; Time-related representativeness (TiR) = 1; Precision (P material) = 1; Precision (P processing) = 1

Time period: Inventory data based on 2023 " Plein Pot Sur les Emballages " (PPSE) data (data from ADEME and Open Food Facts)

Use of "PPSE" data to improve packaging modelling for products not covered by the "PACK AGB" project. Data verified by CTCPA's packaging expert.

General assumptions

For "PPSE" missing data, assumptions are based on CTCPA expertise 
Some multi-layer packaging (identified by CTCPA's expert) are modeled using a packaging solution from PACK AGB project. Nota bene the packaging format may be different.

Assumptions at each stage: 

Production
- Only the packaging material in contact with the product or ensuring the product's shelf life is modeled.
For example, in the case of cookies packaged in PP plastic bags (element 1), themselves packaged in a cardboard box (elements 2): (i) Element 2 is the heaviest / (ii) Element 1 is in contact with the product, so the PP material was taken into account.
- For multi-element and multi-layer packaging, the inventory calls for the material in contact with the product and for the quantity, an assumption has been made to take of the packaging solution (sum of all elements) and consider this value for this material.
- Datasets created as part of the PACK AGB project were used, for the most representative material.

Processing
- Only the most representative process for the most representative packaging material is included.
For example, in the case of a multi-layer flexible film, only the extrusion process is modeled. The lamination process used to combine the various packaging layers was not included. 
- Datasets created as part of the PACK AGB project were used for the most representative process.

Transport
- The assumptions of the PACK AGB project were applied
- Datasets created as part of the PACK AGB project were used, for the most representative packaging material
- Ratios from France and Europe compiled in the PACK AGB project by packaging material were used (ADEME data, 2020).

End of life
- All plastic packaging is considered non-recycled (R2=0%).
To be able to affirm that the plastic packaging is recycled, it is necessary to consider the whole packaging solution (with all the elements and materials) and in this project the dataset only include a part of the packaging (proxy)
- Datasets created as part of the PACK AGB project were used, for the most representative packaging material. 
- The Circular FootPrint Formula was applied.

Vérificateurs : CTCPA (packaging expert from CTCPA)
Contact : Pauline AUDOYE (paudoye@ctcpa.org) ; Mathilde BRAMBATI (mbrambati@ctcpa.org) ; Margaux COLOMBIN(mcolombin@ctcpa.org)

comment:

- Background Ecoinvent data have been updated to Ecoinvent 3.9.1
_________________________________
This dataset represents the global average for wheat grain, at farm. It is calculated as weighted average of the following countries, based on their respective export shares according to FAOSTAT data for 2016:
 - Russia: 14%
 - USA: 13%
 - Canada: 11%
 - France: 10%
 - Australia: 9%
These countries together represent 57% of global export. 
Non-irrigated wheat is assumed for all exporting countries. 

All farming activities documented in the respective national datasets are included. No transportation to the marketplace is considered.
The functional unit is the production of 1 kg of wheat grain with a water content of 15%.

Data quality rating (DQR) = 2.2 (i.e. good quality)

activityName: White asparagus {FR}| white asparagus production | Cut-off, U - Copied from Ecoinvent U
comment:
AGRIBALYSE v3.2 dataset, 2024.
original ecoinvent name: White asparagus {FR}| white asparagus production | Cut-off, U

This dataset represents the production of 1 kg of asparagus. The average Yield_ from 2009 - 2012 is 4.2 t/ha. The data are representative for asparagus production in France. Mineral NPK fertiliser input is 110-50-150 kg/ha. Organic fertilisers applied amount to 0.19 m3/ha of liquid manure and 0.15 t/ha of solid manure. Total active ingredients (a.i.) applied as pesticides amount to 5.66 kg a.i./ha.

The dataset was modelled within the project 'World Food LCA database (WFLDB)'. The aim of this project was to provide inventories of a broad variety of agricultural products and processes and to cover for each product at least 50% of the global export market. The share of asparagus produced in France amounts to 0.2% of the global production (tonnage produced in 2010). The production system regarded in this dataset aimed at representing asparagus produced in France for the export market.

PEF-Quality: data quality rating (DQR) = 1.3 (i.e. excellent quality). This dataset refers to an average situation; for specific situations exchanges might differ substantially due to site specific parameters

Production volume: 20012250 kg
Included activities start: This activity starts with the nursery producing asparagus crown (seedlings).
Included activities end: This activity ends with the removal of asparagus roots after the productive phase (7 years). The dataset includes all activities of a year in a year in the productive phase of the asparagus field including the establishment phase (2 years) per year of lifetime (9 years). 
The establishment phase of the asparagus field includes the nursery, manual planting, soil cultivation (plough), fertilisation (manure) and PE foil. 
The productive phase of the asparagus field includes machine operations, corresponding infrastructure, fuel use and sheds. Machine operations in the productive phase are: soil cultivation, fertiliser and pesticide application, manual harvesting and irrigation. Further, direct field emissions and land use change are included. At the end of the productive phase the field is cleared by removing the asparagus roots.
Heavy metal uptake by the crop is considered.
The inputs of asparagus crowns (seedlings), fertilisers and pesticides as well as packaging of fertilisers and pesticides are considered. The dataset doesn't include emissions from manure storage because these are within the system boundary of animal production.
Energy values: Undefined
Geography: The inventory is modelled for France
Technology level: Current
Technology: Conventional production
Start date: 01/01/2009
End date: 31/12/2022
Is data valid for entire period: True
Time period: 
Macro-economic scenario name: Business-as-Usual

Translated name: Courgette moyenne France, conventionnelle, sortie ferme
Included processes: The inventory includes : (1) the processes of soil preparation and cultivation, sowing, weed control, fertilisation, pest and pathogen control, harvest ; (2) the machines and shed or surface used to park them; (3) all inputs as seed, seedling, fertilizers (mineral and organic), active substances, water for irrigation, fuels as well as the transport to the farm; (4) the direct emissions of the fuel combustion, the abrasion of tyres and the direct emissions on the field.

For more information about this LCI, see the report "Dominique Grasselly, Maëlie Trédan, CTIFL, Vincent Colomb, ADEME, 2017.AGRIBALYSE®fruits et légumes. Compléments à la base de données d'inventaires de cycle de vie et démarche d'écoconception de systèmes de culture, 50p." (english version available)
Direct Land Use Change method (PAS 2050-1:2012) was applied only when CO2 from land transformation is different from 0.

Technological representativeness (TeR) = 2 (good) >=84% and 95%
Geographical representativeness (GR) = 1 (very good) >=95%
Time-related representativeness (TiR) = 2 (good) >=85% and <95%

Methodological appropriateness ans consistency (M) = 2 (good) >=85% and <95%

AGRIBALYSE v3.2 dataset, 2024.
This dataset has been adapted for Agribalyse with recommendations from ACTALIA (september 2022).
- milk is French average
- Yield_ is specific for the type of butter
- parameters add to calculate the amount of coproducts and allocation after Yield_ modification
- cream is deleted
- electricity is French
- Background Ecoinvent data have been updated to Ecoinvent 3.9.1
- Water and waste water is French
_________________________________
Included processes: This multi-output process covers the production of butter, skimmed milk and buttermilk. The butter is unsalted. The inventory includes the inputs of raw milk, energy, water and cleaning agents. Transport of raw milk to the dairy facility is included. Chilled storage of the product at initial warehouse is included. Wastewater treatment and infrastructure are included. Yeast input is included with an empty (""dummy"") dataset. Packaging is not included.
Remark: The functional unit is the production of 1 kg of dairy product. The production system is typical of industrial dairies in Europe. Allocation between co-products is based on their dry matter (DM) content with the following allocation factors: 
 - butter: 33%
 - skimmed milk: 63%
 - buttermilk: 4%

comment:
AGRIBALYSE v3.2 dataset, 2024. 
This dataset has been adapted for Agribalyse 3.2.
- Background Ecoinvent data have been updated to Ecoinvent 3.9.1
_________________________________
"Included processes: This process covers the production of dried pasta from durum wheat. The inventory includes the inputs of durum wheat semolina, energy, water and land occupied by the factory. Transport of durum wheat semolina to the factory is included. Wastes (losses) composting is considered (empty ""dummy"" dataset for composting because of the cut-off allocation method). Packaging is not included.

Remark: The functional unit is the production of 1 kg of durum wheat pasta, unpacked. The production system is based on an Italian factory producing 365'000 tonnes pasta/year. 

Data quality rating (DQR) = 2.2 (i.e. good quality)
"

comment:
AGRIBALYSE v3.2 dataset, 2024.

- Background Ecoinvent data have been updated to Ecoinvent 3.9.1
_________________________________
"The ecoinvent process ""Rape oil, at oil mill/RER U"" is used as a proxy to model Rapseed oil extraction at oil mill.""Rape oil, at oil mill/RER U"" has an oil input of 1.9 kg rapeseed (allocated Yield_).
 Oil Yield_ (unallocated Yield_) was adapted for Rapseed, which amounts to 42.8% (i.e.2.15 kg Rapeseeds are needed for 1 kg Rapeseed oil). For Rapeseed at farm, the global dataset is used.
Economic allocation is applied, based on the price ratio between 1 kg oil and 1.2 kg of the co-product Rapseed oil cake. Price for 1 kg Rapseed oil = 918 US $/t

comment:
AGRIBALYSE v3.2 dataset, 2024. 
This dataset has been adapted for Agribalyse 3.2.
- Background Ecoinvent data have been updated to Ecoinvent 3.9.1
_________________________________
"The SALCA process ""Sunflower oil, at oil mill/kg/CH"" is used as a proxy to model Sunflower oil extraction at oil mill. 

Reference flow: Oil Yield_ (unallocated Yield_): 3.31 kg Sunflower seeds are needed for 1 kg Sunflower oil. For Sunflower at farm, the global dataset is used. Sunflower lecithin Yield_s are assumed to be about 0.3% on a seed basis (Nieuwenhuyzen (2014))

Allocation: economic allocation is applied, based on the price ratio between 1 kg oil, 2.3 kg of the co-product Sunflower oil cake and 0.01 kg sunflower lecithin. Price for 1 kg Sunflower oil = 0.72 US $/pound = 1.58 $/kg

activityName: Apple {CN}| apple production | Cut-off, U
comment:
This dataset represents the production of 1 kg of apples. The average yield from 2009 - 2012 is 16.783 t/ha. The data are representative for apple production in China used for the export market. Mineral NPK fertiliser input is 30-20-40 kg/ha. No organic fertilisers are applied. Total active ingredients (a.i.) applied as pesticides amount to 11.8 kg a.i./ha.

The dataset was modelled within the project 'World Food LCA database (WFLDB)'. The aim of this project was to provide inventories of a broad variety of agricultural products and processes and to cover for each product at least 50% of the global export market. The export share of apples produced in China amounts to 14% of the global export (tonnage exported in 2010). The production system regarded in this dataset aimed at representing apples produced in China for the export market.

PEF-Quality: data quality rating (DQR) = 2.7 (i.e. good quality). This dataset refers to an average situation; for specific situations exchanges might differ substantially due to site specific parameters

Production volume: 3.485720125E10 kg
Included activities start: This activity starts with the nursery producing fruit tree seedlings, i.e. grafted young trees to be planted.
Included activities end: This activity ends with the waste treatment after the clearing of the orchard (rooting up the trees). activityName: Avocado {GLO}| avocado production | Cut-off, U
comment:
This dataset represents avocado production.

Yield: 10 t / ha. 

Duration of one cycle: 12 months in permanent culture

Field production. 

The LCA study, from which this LCI has been derived, contains detailed descriptions of the system boundaries and the data sources used (Stoessel et al. 2012). The publication is published and freely available with comprehensive supporting information:

http://pubs.acs.org/doi/pdf/10.1021/es2030577

Franziska Stoessel, Ronnie Juraske, Stephan Pfister, Stefanie Hellweg. (2012) Life Cycle Inventory and Carbon and Water FoodPrint of Fruits and Vegetables: Application to a Swiss Retailer. Environmental Science & Technology 6(46) 3253-3262.

This activity was adapted to include the global average land use change (LUC) emissions according 2nd edition of the Quantis-modified tool developed by Blonk Consultants 'WFLDB-adapted-Blonk 2014 direct-land-use-change-assessment-tool_2015-05-18a.xlsx', tab. 'Country & land use unknown'. The size of the emission depends on (i) the relative crop expansion in all countries of the crop during the last 20 years and (ii) the corresponding, country specific land transformations. The current results are based on the average FAOSTAT data (harvested area) of 2009-2011 and 1989-1991. The weighted average is used which takes into account relative difference in crop expansion into primary forest, secondary forest, grassland, perennial and annual land.

Production volume: 3.840905E9 kg
Included activities start: From maintenance of the orchards after harvest of the previous crop.
Included activities end: This activity ends with harvest and storage. 
The dataset includes a storage period of 0.9 month and it's use of electricity. The pesticide inputs are classified according to their chemical classes and the emmssions are assigned to the soil (100%). Mercury emissions are neglected due to a lack of data while other heavy metal emissions are included. 
The dataset doesn't include infrastructure for production and storage facilities. No transports for agricultural means of production from the regional storage to the farm are included.
Geography: The inventory is modelled for Global
Technology level: Current
Technology: Production without production standard, but according to GAP

End date: 31/12/2024

activityName: Bell pepper {IN-UP}| bell pepper production, open field | Cut-off, U
comment:
This dataset represents the production of 1 kg of fresh Capsicum during September, 2015-May, 2016 at a farm located in village Bhagatpur Ratan, District Moradabad of Uttar Pradesh State in India. In this area, fields are irrigated with ground water using electric pump for surface irrigation. The farm has a yield of 3000 kg fresh matter per ha for this crop cycle. Sowing date for the crop is 12-October, 2015 and harvesting date is 14-Feburary, 2016. Mineral NP fertilizer input is 245.63-69 kg/ha. Organic fertilizer applied amounts to 60,000 kg of manure from cattle dung. Insecticide used has active ingredient as Carbofuran 450g/ha, Chlorantranilipore 60g/ha (Clothianidin used as proxy), Thiomethoxam 75g/ha, Monocrotophos 540g/ha (Dichlorvos (DDVP) used as proxy). Machinery is used only for soil cultivation with fuel consumption of 12.48 kg/ha using plough and rotary cultivator for soil tillage.   

[This dataset is meant to replace the following datasets:]

Production volume: 8.189E7 kg
Included activities start: This activity starts about twelve weeks after the harvest of the previous crop. The soil is prepared for cultivation in First week of September and sowing of seeds started about five weeks after soil preparation. Thereafter the crop is mature for harvesting in about 4 months.
Included activities end: The activity ends with the harvesting of the mature Capsicum from the Capsicum plant
Geography: The inventory is modelled for India, Uttar Pradesh
Technology level: Current
Technology: Cultivation of Capsicum follows conventional production standards
Start date: 01/01/2015
End date: 31/12/2024
Is data valid for entire period: True
Time period: Soil cultivating date for the main crop: 07-September, 2015; Harvesting date main crop: 14-Feburary, 2016. The soil cultivation, sowing and harvesting dates are taken as the middle date of the week or fortnight told to the data collector by the farmer. Total time from date of sowing to date of harvesting comes to 125 days.  The data is collected for one crop cycle. The cycle of one year is considered for entry in ecoeditor.
Macro-economic scenario name: Business-as-Usual

Sowing date for the crop is 12-October, 2015 and harvesting date is 14-Feburary, 2016. Mineral NP fertilizer input is 245.63-69 kg/ha. Organic fertilizer applied amounts to 60,000 kg of manure from cattle dung. Insecticide used has active ingredient as Carbofuran 450g/ha, Chlorantranilipore 60g/ha (Clothianidin used as proxy), Thiomethoxam 75g/ha, Monocrotophos 540g/ha (Dichlorvos (DDVP) used as proxy). Machinery is used only for soil cultivation with fuel consumption of 12.48 kg/ha using plough and rotary cultivator for soil tillage.

activityName: Chickpea {IN}| chickpea production | Cut-off, U
comment:
This dataset represents the production of 1 kg of fresh Chickpea during September, 2016- January, 2017 at a farm located in village Chandragadh, District Surendranagar of Gujarat. In this area, fields are irrigated using electric pump for surface irrigation. The farm has a yield of 2900 kg fresh matter per ha for this crop cycle. Sowing date for the crop is 02-October, 2016 and harvesting date is 09-January, 2017. Mineral NP fertilizer input is 77-51 kg/ha. Organic fertilizer applied amounts to 14,000 kg of compost from cattle dung. Insecticide used has active ingredient as Dimethoate 104g/ha, Chlorpyrifos 137.55g/ha, Monocrotophos 79.80g/ha. Machinery is used for soil cultivation, other work processes with fuel consumption of 72 kg/ha, and 6.40 kg/ha respectively.

Production volume: 7.18E9 kg
Included activities start: This activity starts about three weeks after the harvest of the previous crop. The soil is prepared for cultivation in third week of September and sowing of seeds started about 10 days after soil preparation. Thereafter the crop is mature for harvesting in about 3 months.


Included activities end: The activity ends with the harvesting of the mature Chickpea (gram in local language) from the Chickpea plant
Geography: The inventory is modelled for India
Technology level: Current
Technology: Cultivation of Chickpea follows conventional production standards
Start date: 01/01/2015
End date: 31/12/2024
Is data valid for entire period: True
Time period: Soil cultivating date for the main crop: 21-September, 2016; Harvesting date main crop: 09-January, 2017. The soil cultivation, sowing and harvesting dates are taken as the middle date of the week or fortnight told to the data collector by the farmer. Total time from date of sowing to date of harvesting comes to 100 days.  The data is collected for one crop cycle. The cycle of one year is considered for entry in ecoeditor.
Macro-economic scenario name: Business-as-Usual

activityName: Cocoa bean {GH}| cocoa bean production, sun-dried | Cut-off, U
comment:
This dataset represents the production of 1 kg of cocoa beans. The reference flow is the average yield per ha and year, from 2009 - 2012: yield (457 kg/ha) obtained under irrigated conditions (total amount of water 1362 m3/ha). The data are representative for cocoa beans production in Ghana used for the export market. Mineral NPK fertiliser input is 0-54-23 kg/ha. No organic fertilisers are applied. Total active ingredients (a.i.) applied as pesticides amount to 7.1 kg a.i./ha.

The dataset was modelled within the project 'World Food LCA database (WFLDB)'. The aim of this project was to provide inventories of a broad variety of agricultural products and processes and to cover for each product at least 50% of the global export market. The export share of cocoa beans produced in Ghana amounts to 10.4 % of the global export (tonnage exported in 2010). The production system regarded in this dataset aimed at representing cocoa beans produced in Ghana for the export market. 

PEF-Quality: data quality rating (DQR) = 1.7 (i.e. very good quality). This dataset refers to an average situation; for specific situations exchanges might differ substantially due to site specific parameters

Production volume: 7.3051075E8 kg
Included activities start: This activity starts with the nursery producing fruit tree seedlings, i.e.grafted young trees to be planted.
Included activities end: This activity ends with the waste treatment after the clearing of the orchard (rooting up the trees). The dataset includes all activities during a year in the productive phase of the orchard including the establishment phase per year of lifetime (50 years), the clearing of the orchard including waste treatment. 
The establishment phase of the orchard includes tree nursery, soil cultivation, planting trees, sowing grass and irrigation. Fertiliser and pesticide use in a year of the establishment phase is assumed to be half of the amount of a year in the productive phase.
The productive phase of the orchard includes fertiliser and pesticide application, harvesting and irrigation. Machine use and infrastructure are excluded as most of the work is assumed to be manual work. Further, direct field emissions and land use change are included. At the end of the productive phase the orchard is cleared by rooting up the trees. On-site fermentation and sun-drying of the cocoa beans are included.
Waste treatment after the clearing of the orchard includes the incineration tree wood. The inputs of seedlings, fertilisers and pesticides as well as packaging of fertilisers and pesticides are considered. Heavy metal uptake by the crop is considered.
Geography: The inventory is modelled for Ghana
Technology level: Current
Technology: Conventional production
Start date: 01/01/2009
End date: 31/12/2024
Is data valid for entire period: True
Macro-economic scenario name: Business-as-Usual

comment:

Included activities start: This activity starts from the reception and storage of feed materials, and dairy herd housing.
Included activities end: This activity ends with the provision of milk at farm, ready-to-deliver. The dataset includes the consumption of feed; the livestock management operations (including bedding, drinking water, milking equipment, cleaning products and water, ammonia and dinitrogen oxyde emissions from housing, and methane emissions from enteric fermentation), manure management emissions; energy and buildings (including electricity for dairying, cattle housing and milk parlour equipment and buildings, and gasoline for regular operations) necessary for the operation of a typical dairy farm. The dataset does not include fodder and feed production and processing into meal for animals, litter production, manure management operations (however, emissions are accounted for); nor milk transportation beyond the farm gate (e.g. to dairy processing plants). Also, the dataset does not include particulate matter emissions, nor any drugs used on the dairy farm, because of the lack of data available on quantities and content. In terms of mass, drugs represent much less than 1% of inputs.

activityName: Fava bean {CA-AB}| fava bean production | Cut-off, U
comment:
This dataset represents the production of 1 tonne of dried fava bean (<16% moisture) during May-August, 2020, at 2089.05 ha faba bean farms located in the Province of Alberta, Canada. Yield values were averaged over 2018-2020, and farms have an average yield of 4598.52 kg grain (<16% moisture) per ha for these crop cycles. The system boundaries include the production of all crop inputs (e.g. seeds, fertilizers, crop protection products, and fuel) and consider nitrogen credits derived from biological N fixation associated with dried faba bean production. Irrigation is included. The sowing date for the crop is May 2020 and the harvesting date is August 2020. The seeding rate is 55.35 kg/tonne of faba bean production. Fertilizer applied contain nitrogen (as N) 1.40 kg/tonne, phosphate (as P2O5) 2.46 kg/tonne, potash (as K2O) 0.90 kg/tonne, and sulfur (as S) 0.31 kg/tonne. Predominant crop protection applied contain active ingredients of glyphosate 0.066 kg/tonne, bentazon 0.064 kg/tonne, and diquat dibromide 0.048 g/tonne. Machinery is used for tillage, seeding, fertilizer application, rolling, herbicide application, fungicide application, harvest aid application, harvesting, and other with total fuel consumption of 7.12 kg/tonne.

Production volume: 9606569.08304765 kg
Included activities start: Starting inputs for this activity include seed, fertilizer, crop protection products and fuel on the farm. This activity begins with soil preparation about 37 weeks after the harvest of the previous crop. The soil is prepared for cultivation in 1st week of May and the sowing of seeds started about 5 days after soil preparation.
Included activities end: This activity ends with faba bean drying to <16% moisture at farm gate. This takes place in August, 19 weeks after the activity start. The activity includes the infrastructures and use of agricultural machinery.
Geography: The inventory is modelled for Alberta
Technology level: Current
Technology: Production of faba bean includes farm practices from tillage, seeding, fertilizer application, rolling, herbicide application, fungicide application, harvest aid application, harvesting, and other field operations, to aeration and drying.
Start date: 01/01/2020
End date: 31/12/2024
Is data valid for entire period: True
Time period: Soil cultivating date for the main crop: May 2020; Harvesting date for the main crop: August 2020. Total time from the date of sowing to the date of harvesting comes to 19 weeks. Yield data were collected and averaged for three crop cycles (2018-2020). All other data were collected for 2020 only.
Macro-economic scenario name: Business-as-Usual

Irrigation is included. The sowing date for the crop is May 2020 and the harvesting date is August 2020. The seeding rate is 82.76 kg/tonne of faba bean production. Fertilizer applied contain nitrogen (as N) 1.67 kg/tonne, phosphate (as P2O5) 3.55 kg/tonne, potash (as K2O) 1.07 kg/tonne, and sulfur (as S) 1.94 kg/tonne. Machinery is used for tillage, seeding, fertilizer application, rolling, herbicide application, fungicide application, harvest aid application, harvesting, and other with total fuel consumption of 9.87 kg/tonne.

Technology level: Current

activityName: Lettuce {GLO}| lettuce production, in heated greenhouse | Cut-off, U
comment:
This dataset represents lettuce production according to the Integrated Production standard in CH.

Yield: 50 t / ha.

Duration of one cropping cycle: 3.4 months.

Greenhouse production.

The LCA study, from which this LCI has been derived, contains detailed descriptions of the system boundaries and the data sources used (Stoessel et al. 2012). The publication is published and freely available with comprehensive supporting information:

http://pubs.acs.org/doi/pdf/10.1021/es2030577

Franziska Stoessel, Ronnie Juraske, Stephan Pfister, Stefanie Hellweg. (2012) Life Cycle Inventory and Carbon and Water FoodPrint of Fruits and Vegetables: Application to a Swiss Retailer. Environmental Science & Technology 6(46) 3253-3262.

This activity was adapted to include the global average land use change (LUC) emissions according 2nd edition of the Quantis-modified tool developed by Blonk Consultants 'WFLDB-adapted-Blonk 2014 direct-land-use-change-assessment-tool_2015-05-18a.xlsx', tab. 'Country & land use unknown'. The size of the emission depends on (i) the relative crop expansion in all countries of the crop during the last 20 years and (ii) the corresponding, country specific land transformations. The current results are based on the average FAOSTAT data (harvested area) of 2009-2011 and 1989-1991. The weighted average is used which takes into account relative difference in crop expansion into primary forest, secondary forest, grassland, perennial and annual land.

Production volume: 2.3622366E10 kg
Included activities start: From seedling production.
Included activities end: This activity ends with harvest and storage. 
The dataset includes a storage period of 0.3 month and it's use of electricity. It also includes the electricity use in the greenhouse. And an average amount of heating energy for the production and the seedling production is included. The pesticide inputs are classified according to their chemical classes and the emmssions are assigned to the soil (100%). Mercury emissions are neglected due to a lack of data while other heavy metal emissions are included. The dataset doesn't include infrastructure for production and storage facilities. No transports for agricultural means of production from the regional storage to the farm are included.
Geography: The inventory is modelled for Global
Technology level: Current
Technology: Integrated Production
Start date: 01/01/2010
End date: 31/12/2024
Is data valid for entire period: True
Macro-economic scenario name: Business-as-Usual

activityName: Mint {IN}| mint production | Cut-off, U
comment:
This dataset represents the production of 1 kg mint. The average yield from 1999 is 16.5 t/ha. The data are representative for mint production in India, Uttar Pradesh, used for the export market. Mineral NPK fertiliser input is 160-50-50 kg/ha. No organic fertilisers are applied. Total active ingredients (a.i.) applied as pesticides amount to 0.74 kg a.i./ha.

The dataset was modelled within the project 'World Food LCA database (WFLDB)'. The aim of this project was to provide inventories of a broad variety of agricultural products and processes and to cover for each product at least 50% of the global export market. The production system regarded in this dataset aimed at representing mint produced in India for the export market.

PEF-Quality: data quality rating (DQR) = 2.7 (i.e. good quality). This dataset refers to an average situation; for specific situations exchanges might differ substantially due to site specific parameters

Production volume: 6.0E9 kg
Included activities start: This activity starts with the nursery producing seedlings, i.e. seedlings from roots.
Included activities end: This activity ends with the clearing of the field (removing of mint plants). The dataset includes all activities of a year in the productive phase of the field including the establishment phase per year of lifetime (4 years), and the clearing of the field. 
The establishment phase of the field includes seedlings nursery, soil cultivation, planting, herbicide use and irrigation.
The productive phase of the field includes machine operations, fuel use and sheds. Machine operations in the productive phase are: soil cultivation, fertiliser and pesticide application, harvesting, transport on farm and irrigation. Further, direct field emissions and land use change are included. At the end of the productive phase the field is cleared by removing the mint plants.
Heavy metal uptake by the crop is considered. The inputs of seedlings, fertilisers and pesticides as well as packaging of fertilisers and pesticides are considered. The dataset doesn't include drying.
Geography: The inventory is modelled for India
Technology level: Current
Technology: Conventional production
Start date: 01/01/1999
End date: 31/12/2024
Is data valid for entire period: True
Time period: Time period referring to the data source: 1999-1999. Based on expert opinion data is considered to be valid at least up to 2012.
Macro-economic scenario name: Business-as-Usual

activityName: Orange, fresh grade {US}| orange production, fresh grade | Cut-off, U
comment:
This dataset represents the production of 1 kg of orange, fresh grade (Navelina). Fresh grade oranges are meant for direct human consumption. The reference flow is the average yield per ha and year, from 2010 - 2014: yield (32 t/ha) obtained under irrigated conditions (total amount of water 4457 m3/ha). The data are representative for orange production, fresh grade (Navel), in the United States (California) used for the export market. Mineral NPK fertiliser input is 95-38-45 kg/ha. No organic fertilisers are applied. Total active ingredients (a.i.) applied as pesticides amount to 11 kg a.i./ha and 8.8 kg/ha of horticultural oil.

The dataset was modelled within the project 'World Food LCA database (WFLDB)'. The aim of this project was to provide inventories of a broad variety of agricultural products and processes and to cover for each product at least 50% of the global export market. The export share of fresh grade oranges produced in the United States amounts to 10.3% of the global export (tonnage exported in 2010). The production system regarded in this dataset aimed at representing fresh grade oranges produced in the United Staes or the export market.

PEF-Quality: data quality rating (DQR) = 1.2 (i.e. excellent quality). This dataset refers to an average situation; for specific situations exchanges might differ substantially due to site specific parameters

Production volume: 2.13475E9 kg
Included activities start: This activity starts with the nursery producing fruit tree seedlings, i.e.grafted young trees to be planted.
Included activities end: This activity ends with the waste treatment after the clearing of the orchard (rooting up the trees). The dataset includes all activities during a year in the productive phase of the orchard including the establishment phase per year of lifetime (20 years), the clearing of the orchard including waste treatment. 
The establishment phase of the orchard includes tree nursery, soil cultivation, planting trees, sowing grass, installation of trellis system (posts and wires) and irrigation. Fertiliser and pesticide use in a year of the establishment phase is assumed to be half of the amount of a year in the productive phase.
The productive phase of the orchard includes machine operations, corresponding infrastructure, fuel use and sheds. Machine operations in the productive phase are: soil cultivation (mulching, mowing), fertiliser and pesticide application, harvesting and irrigation. Further, direct field emissions and land use change are included. At the end of the productive phase the orchard is cleared by rooting up the trees.
The inputs of seedlings, fertilisers and pesticides as well as packaging of fertilisers and pesticides are considered. The dataset doesn't include emissions from manure storage because these are within the system boundary of animal production.  Heavy metal uptake by the crop is considered.
Geography: The inventory is modelled for United States of America
Technology level: Current
Technology: Conventional production
Start date: 01/01/2010
End date: 31/12/2024
Is data valid for entire period: True
Macro-economic scenario name: Business-as-Usual

activityName: Pea {CH}| pea production, conventional, hill region | Cut-off, U
comment:
This dataset represents the production of 1 kg of peas calculated on a sectoral average of the production of 1 ha with a yield of 5297 kg at a moisture content of 92.0%. The yield is based on average yield from 2017-2021 in Agristat corrected by region and production system differences in AGRIDEA (2021). "Deckungsbeiträge Ausgabe 2021." Lindau, Agridea, Fibl.. Modelled crop duration is 3.9 months, preceeded by 7.5 months of non-hibernating green manure crop. The data are representative for conventional peas production under tillage in the Swiss hill region. Mineral fertiliser input is 15 kg N, 42 kg P2O5, 159 kg K2O, 1.5 kg Mg. No farm manure has been applied. No organic market fertiliser has been applied.  This dataset was modelled under the aim of a sectoral view on the Swiss Agriculture. The active ingredients applied for plant protection resemble a weighted average mix per crop and not an actual practice on a single farm. Pesticide data from 2018-2020 has been used, originating from the Swiss Agri-Environmental Data Network (SAEDN) (Gilgen et al. 2023). Similarly, farm manure application has been estimated by applying a basic distribution per crop and production system (0% of P2O5 requirement covered with farm manure, based on AGRIDEA 2021) and correcting for the available amount of farm manure in Switzerland that needs to be spread on the cultivated area. The remaining nutrient requirement of the crop is then covered by mineral fertiliser. Machinery operations used for the SALCA emission modelling are taken from  www.labourscope.ch (Accessed: May 2024) ( Groher, T., Heitkämper, K., Umstätter, C. (2020). "Stand der Mechanisierung in der Schweizer Landwirtschaft: Teil 1: Pflanzenproduktion." Agroscope Transfer, 351, 2020, 1-123.), an application for calculating the working-time requirement of labour and production processes (www. www.labourscope.ch (Accessed: May 2024).ch). For the respective inventory modelling, ecoinvent field work processes are used.

Production volume: 1.2612767E7 kg
Included activities start: This activity starts after the harvest of the previous crop. A non-hibernating green manure crop is modelled between harvest of the previous crop and soil cultivation of the current crop. Included inputs are seeds (crop and green manure), mineral fertilizer and plant protection products. Activities of soil cultivation, sowing, fertilizer application, farm manure spreading, pest and pathogen control, weed control and harvest are included. Irrigation is included as well.
Included activities end: This activity ends with harvest and transport to the farm gate (2km). Storage and drying of harvest goods/grains not included.
Geography: The inventory is modelled for Switzerland
Technology level: Current
Technology: Conventional production
Start date: 01/01/2017
End date: 31/12/2024
Is data valid for entire period: True
Time period: 2017-2023: Yield data have been collected for the years 2017-2021. For Fertilisation, data sources are taken from the years 2017-2022, Pesticide data are used from the years 2018-2020, and Machinery and workprocess data from 2018.
Macro-economic scenario name: Business-as-Usual

activityName: Peanut {BR-SP}| peanut production, in cropping system | Cut-off, U
comment:
The raw data collected in interviews were organized in electronic spreadsheets and checked for completeness and consistency. Agricultural inputs were detailed as to their composition and physical characteristics. Agricultural operations were characterized in terms type of fuel and specific consumption. Precipitation is enought to supply water to the crop, no extra water needed. Emissions from the agricultural process were estimated using the BRCalc/ICVCalc tool, developed by Embrapa Environment, which includes specific climate and soil databases for the 137 Brazilian agricultural mesoregions, in addition to databases of parameters related to agricultural crops, fertilisers and pesticides.

The main emission models adopted by BRCalc/ICVCalc (Folegatti-Matsuura et al., 2022) derive from the references: Nemecek et al. (2015), IPCC (2019), Nemecek & Kagi (2007), Folegatti-Matsuura & Picoli (2018). It was used the model BRLUC (Donke et al., 2020) to estimate the LUC emissions; and the PestLCI Consensus V1.0, parameterized for Brazil, to estimate pesticide emissions.

Synonym:
peanut production, peanut cultivation
Production volume: 4.82279E8 kg
Included activities start: This activity starts with soil preparation (reforming) after the last pasture grazing or harvest of the previous crop (sugarcane).
Included activities end: The dataset includes the inputs of correctives, mineral fertilisers and pesticides. It is assumed that no organic fertiliser is applied. The dataset includes the amount of fuel consumed during agricultural operations and their emissions are estimated. The dataset also includes direct field emissions and land use change emissions, with important regionalizations added. The dataset doesn't include: seed inputs, cleaning and storage of harvested grains. The activity ends after harvest at the farm gate.
Geography: The inventory is modelled for Brazil, São Paulo
Technology level: Current
Technology: This dataset represents the production of 1 kg of peanut in shell (fresh matter) composed of 77% grains/kernel, 23% of shell, in the Alta Paulista and the Alta Mogiana regions in the state of Sao Paulo, which is composed of the peanut production regions of Marilia, Tupã and Ribeirão Preto. This is an averaged dataset which includes 1 scenario in rotation with pasture and 3 in rotation with sugarcane of which one is ripstrip. When in a cropping system, land occupation, soil preparation operation, correctives application and correctives, liming operation and limestone are allocated among the products of the system, adopting factors that consider the fraction of area and the occupation time. In this case, 4% of total correctives and 4% of diesel used in the agricultural operations that were shared with pasture/sugarcane were considered as input for peanut production. Mineral fertiliser input is 130 kg MAP/ha and 69.9 kg KCl/ha. Total active ingredients (a.i.) applied as pesticides amount to 14.91 kg a.i./ha. In the ripstrip scenario, Ripstrip was used during soil preparation, reducing the diesel consumption. The average productivity is 4554 kg/ha, at 11% moisture.

Agricultural operation was modelled based on the total diesel consumed to perform the operation and the emissions to air related to diesel burning.

All inputs are averaged by the production volumes of the regions.
Start date: 01/01/2020
End date: 31/12/2024
Is data valid for entire period: True
Time period: Time period of the most of the data collected for this dataset.
Macro-economic scenario name: Business-as-Usual

The comments below were part of the CN regional dataset.

This dataset represents the production of 1 kg of pear. The average yield from 2009 - 2012 is 13.9 t/ha. The data are representative for pear production in China used for the export market. Mineral NPK fertiliser input is 150-40-40 kg/ha. Organic fertilisers applied amount to 1.11 m3/ha of liquid manure and 0.88 t/ha of solid manure. Total active ingredients (a.i.) applied as pesticides amount to 11.82 kg a.i./ha.

The dataset was modelled within the project 'World Food LCA database (WFLDB)'. The aim of this project was to provide inventories of a broad variety of agricultural products and processes and to cover for each product at least 50% of the global export market. The export share of pear produced in China amounts to 17% of the global export (tonnage exported in 2010). The production system regarded in this dataset aimed at representing pear produced in China for the export market.

PEF-Quality: data quality rating (DQR) = 3.0 (i.e. good quality). This dataset refers to an average situation; for specific situations exchanges might differ substantially due to site specific parameters

Production volume: 5.47439625E9 kg
Included activities start: This activity starts with the nursery producing fruit tree seedlings, i.e. grafted young trees to be planted.
Included activities end: This activity ends with the waste treatment after the clearing of the orchard (rooting up the trees). The dataset includes all activities of a year in a year in the productive phase of the orchard including the establishment phase per year of lifetime (20 years, 1250 trees/ha planted), the clearing of the orchard including waste treatment. 
The establishment phase of the orchard includes tree nursery, soil cultivation, planting trees, sowing grass, installation of trellis system (posts and wires) and irrigation. Fertiliser and pesticide use in a year of the establishment phase is assumed to be half of the amount of a year in the productive phase.
The productive phase of the orchard includes machine operations, corresponding infrastructure, fuel use and sheds. Machine operations in the productive phase are: soil cultivation (mulching, mowing), fertiliser and pesticide application, harvesting and irrigation. Further, direct field emissions and land use change are included. At the end of the productive phase the orchard is cleared by rooting up the trees.
Heavy metal uptake by the crop is considered.
The inputs of seedlings, fertilisers and pesticides as well as packaging of fertilisers and pesticides are considered. fertilisers and pesticides are considered. The dataset doesn't include emissions from manure storage because these are within the system boundary of animal production.
Statistical data from FAO used to assess land use change is incomplete for China. The original land use of 40.9% of annual cropland and 100% of perennial cropland transformed in the last 20 years is unknown. Land use change impacts may therefore be underestimated.

Franziska Stoessel, Ronnie Juraske, Stephan Pfister, Stefanie Hellweg. (2012) Life Cycle Inventory and Carbon and Water FoodPrint of Fruits and Vegetables: Application to a Swiss Retailer. Environmental Science & Technology 6(46) 3253?3262.

The weighted average is used which takes into account relative difference in crop expansion into primary forest, secondary forest, grassland, perennial and annual land.

No transports for agricultural means of production from the regional storage to the farm are included.

activityName: Red kidney bean {CA-ON}| red kidney bean production | Cut-off, U
comment:
This dataset represents the production of 1 tonne of dried red kidney bean (<15% moisture) during May-September, 2020, at 1765.24 ha red kidney bean farms located in the Province of Ontario, Canada. Yield values were averaged over 2018-2020, and farms have an average yield of 2696.50 kg grain (<15% moisture) per ha for these crop cycles. The system boundaries include the production of all crop inputs (e.g. seeds, fertilizers, crop protection products, and fuel) and consider nitrogen credits derived from biological N fixation associated with dried red kidney bean production. Irrigation is included. The sowing date for the crop is May 2020 and the harvesting date is September 2020. The seeding rate is 33.40 kg/tonne of red kidney bean production. Fertilizer applied contain nitrogen (as N) 18.25 kg/tonne, phosphate (as P2O5) 8.29 kg/tonne, potash (as K2O) 24.09 kg/tonne, and sulfur (as S) 2.48 kg/tonne. Predominant crop protection applied contain active ingredients of glyphosate 0.018 kg/tonne, bentazon 0.13 kg/tonne, and prothiconazole 0.018 kg/tonne. Machinery is used for tillage, fertilizer application, pre-plant herbicide application, planting, rolling, post-emergent herbicide application, inter-row cultivating/scuffing/hilling, fungicide application, pre-harvest desiccation, pull/undercut/knife, windrow/swathing, harvesting, and other with total fuel consumption of 21.03 kg/tonne.

Production volume: 4759970.555238 kg
Included activities start: Starting inputs for this activity include seed, fertilizer, crop protection products and fuel on the farm. This activity begins with soil preparation about 39 weeks after the harvest of the previous crop. The soil is prepared for cultivation in last week of May and the sowing of seeds started about 5 days after soil preparation.
Included activities end: This activity ends with navy bean drying to <15% moisture at farm gate. This takes place in September, 17 weeks after the activity starts. The activity includes the infrastructures and use of agricultural machinery

Geography: The inventory is modelled for Ontario
Technology level: Current
Technology: Production of red kidney bean includes farm practices from tillage, fertilizer application, pre-plant herbicide application, planting, rolling, post-emergent herbicide application, inter-row cultivating/scuffing/hilling, fungicide application, pre-harvest desiccation, pull/undercut/knife, windrow/swathing, harvesting, and other field activities, to aeration and drying.
Start date: 01/01/2020
End date: 31/12/2024

activityName: Spinach {CH}| spinach production, conventional, plain region | Cut-off, U
comment:
This dataset represents the production of 1 kg of spinach calculated on a sectoral average of the production of 1 ha with a yield of 16727 kg at a moisture content of 92.0%. The yield is based on average yield from 2017-2021 in Agristat corrected by region and production system differences in AGRIDEA (2021). Modelled crop duration is 1.8 months, preceeded by 8.2 months of non-hibernating green manure crop. The data are representative for conventional spinach production under tillage in the Swiss plain region. Mineral fertiliser input is 190 kg N, 35 kg P2O5, 279 kg K2O, 2.7 kg Mg. No farm manure has been applied. No organic market fertiliser has been applied.  This dataset was modelled under the aim of a sectoral view on the Swiss Agriculture. The active ingredients applied for plant protection resemble a weighted average mix per crop and not an actual practice on a single farm. Pesticide data from 2018-2020 has been used, originating from the Swiss Agri-Environmental Data Network (SAEDN) (Gilgen et al. 2023). Similarly, farm manure application has been estimated by applying a basic distribution per crop and production system (0% of P2O5 requirement covered with farm manure, based on AGRIDEA 2021) and correcting for the available amount of farm manure in Switzerland that needs to be spread on the cultivated area. The remaining nutrient requirement of the crop is then covered by mineral fertiliser. Machinery operations used for the SALCA emission modelling are taken from  www.labourscope.ch (Accessed: May 2024) ( Groher, T., Heitkämper, K., Umstätter, C. (2020). "Stand der Mechanisierung in der Schweizer Landwirtschaft: Teil 1: Pflanzenproduktion." Agroscope Transfer, 351, 2020, 1-123.), an application for calculating the working-time requirement of labour and production processes (www. www.labourscope.ch (Accessed: May 2024).ch). For the respective inventory modelling, ecoinvent field work processes are used.

Production volume: 2.7444326E7 kg
Included activities start: This activity starts after the harvest of the previous crop. A non-hibernating green manure crop is modelled between harvest of the previous crop and soil cultivation of the current crop. Included inputs are seeds (crop and green manure), mineral fertilizer and plant protection products. Activities of soil cultivation, sowing, fertilizer application, farm manure spreading, pest and pathogen control, weed control and harvest are included. Irrigation is included as well.
Included activities end: This activity ends with harvest and transport to the farm gate (2km). Storage and drying of harvest goods/grains not included.
Geography: The inventory is modelled for Switzerland
Technology level: Current
Technology: Conventional production
Start date: 01/01/2017
End date: 31/12/2024
Is data valid for entire period: True
Time period: 2017-2023: Yield data have been collected for the years 2017-2021. For Fertilisation, data sources are taken from the years 2017-2022, Pesticide data are used from the years 2018-2020, and Machinery and workprocess data from 2018.
Macro-economic scenario name: Business-as-Usual

activityName: Strawberry {US}| strawberry production, open field, macro tunnel | Cut-off, U
comment:
This dataset represents the production of 1 kg of strawberry. The reference flow is the average national yield per ha and for the year 2010: yield (56.2 t/ha.y) obtained under irrigated conditions (total amount of water 9144 m3/ha.y). The data are representative for strawberry production in the United States (California) used for the export market. Mineral NPK fertiliser input is 197-117-140 kg/ha. No organic fertilisers are applied. Total active ingredients (a.i.) applied as various pesticides amount to 93.7 kg a.i./ha and 51.9 kg chloropicrin/ha.

The dataset was modelled within the project 'World Food LCA database (WFLDB)'. The aim of this project was to provide inventories of a broad variety of agricultural products and processes and to cover for each product at least 50% of the global export market. The export share of strawberries produced in the United States amounts to 17 % of the global export (tonnage exported in 2010). The production system regarded in this dataset aimed at representing strawberries produced in open fields in the United States for the export market.

PEF-Quality: data quality rating (DQR) = 2.0 (i.e. very good quality). This dataset refers to an average situation; for specific situations exchanges might differ substantially due to site specific parameters

Production volume: 1.31E9 kg
Included activities start: This activity starts with soil cultivation after the harvest of the previous crop.
Included activities end: This activity ends with harvest and transport to the farm gate. Storage is not included. 
The dataset includes all activities during a cycle, i.e. all machine operations, corresponding infrastructure, fuel use and sheds. Machine operations include: soil cultivation, fertilisation, pesticide application, harvesting, and on-farm transport. Further, direct field emissions and land use change are included. Irrigation is included. The inputs of seedlings, fertilisers and pesticides as well as packaging of fertilisers and pesticides are considered. Heavy metal uptake by the crop is considered.

Geography: The inventory is modelled for United States of America
Technology level: Current
Technology: Conventional production
Start date: 01/01/2010
End date: 31/12/2024
Is data valid for entire period: True
Macro-economic scenario name: Business-as-Usual

activityName: Sweet corn {US-MN}| sweet corn production | Cut-off, U
comment:
This dataset represents the production of 1 kg of Sweet Corn (fresh matter) in the US state of Minnesota at farm, with an at harvest moisture content of 76.%. This dataset includes cultivation of the field prior to planting, field treatments, planting, applications of nutrients and pesticides, and harvest. Residues are not collected but remain on the field post-harvest and overwinter.

The average yield of Sweet Corn grown in Minnesota for the 2014-2021 seasons was 16,813 kg/ha (wet mass) (USDA NASS (2022a)).  The dataset reflects the average Sweet Corn produced in Minnesota from 2014 to 2021, inclusive, as that period allows for at least one value from USDA statistics for most parameters and generally three or more.  Seed establishment and weed control for sweet corn generally require tillage (EPA 2022; IPM 2003, IPM 1997), so this dataset reflects sweet corn production using conventional tillage practices (0% no till, 0% reduced till, 100% conventional tillage) (EPA 2022; IPM center 2003; IPM center 1997 data) and being grown in rotations with other vegetable crops. While genetically engineered sweet (fresh) corn seed is available, the share of sweet (fresh) corn grown from genetically engineered seed is not compiled; it is estimated that between 75 and 90% of North American sweet corn is conventional (USDA 2018b).

Area, productivity, use of mineral and organic fertilisers and pesticides, and irrigation inputs are based on farmer data reported to the U.S. Department of Agriculture where possible or budgets available for the state, unless otherwise noted. Field operations and equipment types and fuel use are based on materials provided to growers by the agricultural extension office(s), including farm budgets, and on survey information agricultural extension office(s) collect from growers, in conjunction with row spacing data from USDA.  57.6% of crop land has installed drainage (tile or ditch), based on state-level agricultural survey data from USDA.  Irrigation is included based on share of crop irrigated (13.5% over the time period, USDA NASS (2018d)).

Total cropland land use, for all crops, in Minnesota increased by 1% between 1997 and 2017 (NRCS 2020); USDA NASS does not report cropped area for Sweet Corn prior to 2016.

Soil characteristics, including pH, are based on distribution of soil pH sampling results reported in the 2020 Soil Test Summary (Bruulsema and Jones 2021). The share of acidic soils is likely overestimated as more frequent testing is to be expected on soils having needed lime and thus low pH soils are likely to be more represented amongst the collected samples. No anti-erosion practices are assumed in the dataset; instead, the erosion soil loss reported in the U.S. Natural Resources Conservation Service's Natural Resource Inventory is used.

References:

USDA NASS (2022a) Area, Production, Yield by State - Sweet Corn - 2016-2022. US Department of Agriculture (USDA) National Agricultural Statistics Service. https://quickstats.nass.usda.gov (direct query: https://quickstats.nass.usda.gov/results/5E5B411A-F9EF-3B83-AAFF-995DD89820FC)

USDA NASS (2018b) Statistical Methodology Name of Survey: Agricultural Resource Management Survey (ARMS) Phase II: PeanutProduction Practices Report, CornProduction Practices Report, and Soybean Production Practices Cost Report. US Department of Agriculture (USDA). https://www.nass.usda.gov/Surveys/Guide_to_NASS_Surveys/Chemical_Use/2018_Peanuts_Soybeans_Corn/Statistical%20Methodology%202018.pdf

IPM center (1997) Crop Profile for Corn (Sweet) in Maryland. Southern Integrated Pest Management Center. https://ipmdata.ipmcenters.org/documents/cropprofiles/MDcorn-sweet.pdf

IPM center (2003) Crop Profile for Sweet Corn in the North Central United States. Southern Integrated Pest Management Center.Southern Integrated Pest Management Center. https://ipmdata.ipmcenters.org/documents/cropprofiles/us-ncr-sweetcorn.pdf

Included activities start: This activity starts with the nursery producing tree seedlings, i.e. grafted young trees to be planted.
Included activities end: This activity ends with the waste treatment after the clearing of the orchard (rooting up the trees). The dataset includes all activities of a year in a year in the productive phase of the orchard including the establishment phase per year of lifetime (20 years), and the clearing of the orchard including waste treatment. 
The establishment phase of the orchard includes tree nursery, soil cultivation, planting trees, sowing grass, installation of trellis system (posts and wires) and irrigation. Fertiliser and pesticide use in a year of the establishment phase is assumed to be half of the amount of a year in the productive phase.
The productive phase of the orchard includes machine operations, corresponding infrastructure, fuel use and sheds. Machine operations in the productive phase are: fertiliser and pesticide application, and irrigation. Further, direct field emissions and land use change are included. At the end of the productive phase the orchard is cleared by rooting up the trees.
   Heavy metal uptake by the crop is considered.
The inputs of seedlings, fertilisers and pesticides as well as packaging of fertilisers and pesticides are considered. 
Statistical data from FAO used to assess land use change is incomplete for China. The original land use of 40.9% of annual cropland and 100% of perennial cropland transformed in the last 20 years is unknown. Land use change impacts may therefore be underestimated.

comment:
This is a market activity. Each market represents the consumption mix of a product in a given geography, connecting suppliers with consumers of the same product in the same geographical area. Markets group the producers and also the imports of the product (if relevant) within the same geographical area. They also account for transport to the consumer and for the losses during that process, when relevant.

This dataset represents the supply of textile, non-woven polyester from activities that produce it within the geography of this dataset.

The transport amounts are based on the default transport distances for markets, provided in the 'Default Transport Assumptions' file available on the ecoinvent website (https://www.ecoinvent.org/support/documents-and-files/documents-and-files.html). See exchange comments for additional details.

comment:
This dataset represents the production of 1 kg of asparagus. The average yield from 2009 - 2012 is 5.3 t/ha. The data are representative for asparagus production in China for the export market based on average data over the country. Mineral NPK fertiliser input is 80-60-40 kg/ha. Organic fertilisers applied amount to 0.17 m3/ha of liquid manure and 0.14 t/ha of solid manure. Total active ingredients (a.i.) applied as pesticides amount to 3.6 kg a.i./ha.

The dataset was modelled within the project 'World Food LCA database (WFLDB)'. The aim of this project was to provide inventories of a broad variety of agricultural products and processes and to cover for each product at least 50% of the global export market. The share of asparagus produced in China amounts to 88% of the global production (tonnage produced in 2010). The production system regarded in this dataset aimed at representing asparagus produced in China for the export market.

PEF-Quality: data quality rating (DQR) = 2.8 (i.e. good quality). This dataset refers to an average situation; for specific situations exchanges might differ substantially due to site specific parameters

Production volume: 6.927883E9 kg
Included activities start: This activity starts with the nursery producing asparagus crown (seedlings).
Included activities end: This activity ends with the removal of asparagus roots after the productive phase (7 years). The dataset includes all activities of a year in a year in the productive phase of the asparagus field including the establishment phase (2 years) per year of lifetime (9 years). 
The establishment phase of the asparagus field includes the nursery, manual planting, soil cultivation (plough), fertilisation (manure) and PE foil. 
The productive phase of the asparagus field includes machine operations, corresponding infrastructure, fuel use and sheds. Machine operations in the productive phase are: soil cultivation, fertiliser and pesticide application, manual harvesting and irrigation. Further, direct field emissions and land use change are included. At the end of the productive phase the field is cleared by removing the asparagus roots.
Heavy metal uptake by the crop is considered.
The inputs of asparagus crowns (seedlings), fertilisers and pesticides as well as packaging of fertilisers and pesticides are considered. The dataset doesn't include emissions from manure storage because these are within the system boundary of animal production.  Heavy metal uptake by the crop is considered.
Statistical data from FAO used to assess land use change is incomplete for China. The original land use of 40.9% of annual cropland and 100% of perennial cropland transformed in the last 20 years is unknown. Land use change impacts may therefore be underestimated.
