activityName: White cabbage {CH}| white cabbage production, conventional, plain region | Cut-off, U
comment:
This dataset represents the production of 1 kg of cabbage calculated on a sectoral average of the production of 1 ha with a yield of 24487 kg at a moisture content of 92.0%. The yield is based on average yield from 2017-2021 in Agristat corrected by region and production system differences in AGRIDEA (2021). Modelled crop duration is 4.9 months, preceeded by 10.2 months of non-hibernating green manure crop. The data are representative for conventional cabbage production under tillage in the Swiss plain region. Mineral fertiliser input is 92 kg N, 37 kg P2O5, 122 kg K2O, 1.2 kg Mg. No farm manure has been applied. No organic market fertiliser has been applied.  This dataset was modelled under the aim of a sectoral view on the Swiss Agriculture. The active ingredients applied for plant protection resemble a weighted average mix per crop and not an actual practice on a single farm. Pesticide data from 2018-2020 has been used, originating from the Swiss Agri-Environmental Data Network (SAEDN) (Gilgen et al. 2023). Similarly, farm manure application has been estimated by applying a basic distribution per crop and production system (0% of P2O5 requirement covered with farm manure, based on AGRIDEA 2021) and correcting for the available amount of farm manure in Switzerland that needs to be spread on the cultivated area. The remaining nutrient requirement of the crop is then covered by mineral fertiliser. Machinery operations used for the SALCA emission modelling are taken from  www.labourscope.ch (Accessed: May 2024) ( Groher, T., Heitkämper, K., Umstätter, C. (2020). "Stand der Mechanisierung in der Schweizer Landwirtschaft: Teil 1: Pflanzenproduktion." Agroscope Transfer, 351, 2020, 1-123.), an application for calculating the working-time requirement of labour and production processes (www. www.labourscope.ch (Accessed: May 2024).ch). For the respective inventory modelling, ecoinvent field work processes are used.

Production volume: 2.578234E7 kg
Included activities start: This activity starts after the harvest of the previous crop. A non-hibernating green manure crop is modelled between harvest of the previous crop and soil cultivation of the current crop. Included inputs are seeds (crop and green manure), mineral fertilizer and plant protection products. Activities of soil cultivation, sowing, fertilizer application, farm manure spreading, pest and pathogen control, weed control and harvest are included. Irrigation is included as well.
Included activities end: This activity ends with harvest and transport to the farm gate (2km). Storage and drying of harvest goods/grains not included.
Geography: The inventory is modelled for Switzerland
Technology level: Current
Technology: Conventional production

End date: 31/12/2024

The data are representative for conventional zucchini production under tillage in the Swiss plain region. Mineral fertiliser input is 81 kg N, 16 kg P2O5, 81 kg K2O, 0.5 kg Mg. No farm manure has been applied. No organic market fertiliser has been applied.  This dataset was modelled under the aim of a sectoral view on the Swiss Agriculture. The active ingredients applied for plant protection resemble a weighted average mix per crop and not an actual practice on a single farm. Pesticide data from 2018-2020 has been used, originating from the Swiss Agri-Environmental Data Network (SAEDN) (Gilgen et al. 2023). Similarly, farm manure application has been estimated by applying a basic distribution per crop and production system (0% of P2O5 requirement covered with farm manure, based on AGRIDEA 2021) and correcting for the available amount of farm manure in Switzerland that needs to be spread on the cultivated area. The remaining nutrient requirement of the crop is then covered by mineral fertiliser. Machinery operations used for the SALCA emission modelling are taken from  www.labourscope.ch (Accessed: May 2024) ( Groher, T., Heitkämper, K., Umstätter, C. (2020). "Stand der Mechanisierung in der Schweizer Landwirtschaft: Teil 1: Pflanzenproduktion." Agroscope Transfer, 351, 2020, 1-123.), an application for calculating the working-time requirement of labour and production processes (www. www.labourscope.ch (Accessed: May 2024).ch). For the respective inventory modelling, ecoinvent field work processes are used.

Production volume: 1.227177E7 kg
Included activities start: This activity starts after the harvest of the previous crop. A non-hibernating green manure crop is modelled between harvest of the previous crop and soil cultivation of the current crop. Included inputs are seeds (crop and green manure), mineral fertilizer and plant protection products. Activities of soil cultivation, sowing, fertilizer application, farm manure spreading, pest and pathogen control, weed control and harvest are included. Irrigation is included as well.
Included activities end: This activity ends with harvest and transport to the farm gate (2km). Storage and drying of harvest goods/grains not included.
Geography: The inventory is modelled for Switzerland
Technology level: Current
Technology: Conventional production

End date: 31/12/2024
Is data valid for entire period: True
Time period: 2017-2023: Yield data have been collected for the years 2017-2021. For Fertilisation, data sources are taken from the years 2017-2022, Pesticide data are used from the years 2018-2020, and Machinery and workprocess data from 2018.

'Country & land use unknown'. The size of the emission depends on (i) the relative crop expansion in all countries of the crop during the last 20 years and (ii) the corresponding, country specific land transformations. The current results are based on the average FAOSTAT data (harvested area) of 2009-2011 and 1989-1991. Direct field emissions from crop production activities and from land use change are considered. The establishment phase of the orchard, i.e. tree nursery, soil cultivation, planting trees, sowing grass, installation of trellis system (posts and wires) and irrigation. Fertiliser and pesticide use in a year of the establishment phase is assumed to be half of the amount of a year in the productive phase. 
Remark: The functional unit is the production of 1 kg of apples. The reference flow is the average yield per ha and year for the reference period of 2009 - 2012: yield (16.783 t/ha) obtained under irrigated conditions (total amount of water 12249 m3/ha). System boundary: an average year of the productive phase is regarded; included are also the per year of lifetime calculated emissions for nursery, materials for planting, establishment and clearing phase; at farm without storage. Number of years from planting to clearing (lifetime): 15 years   - Waste treatment after clearing of the orchard: Wooden posts and tree wood go to incineration, concrete posts go to land fill, iron wires go to recycling. The data are representative for apple production in China used for the export market.

Data quality rating (DQR) = 2.5 (i.e. good quality)

activityName: Asparagus, at farm (WFLDB)
comment:
Translated name: Asparagus, at farm
Included processes: The inventory includes all activites of an average year in the productive phase of an asparagus field, i.e. soil cultivation, pesticide application, fertilisation and harvesting (manually). Machine infrastructure including a shed for shelter and fuel use are also considered as well as transport on farm. Inputs of fertilisers, pesticides, irrigation water and seedlings are included. Direct field emissions from crop production activities (e.g. fertiliser and pesticide use) and land use change are considered. Also regarded are the first two years of the non-productive phase, i.e.planting (manually), soil cultivation (plough), fertilisation (manure) and PE foil.
Remark: The functional unit is the production of 1 kg of asparagus. The reference flow is the average yield per ha and year for the reference period of 2009 - 2012 (i.e. 5.3 t/ha) obtained under irrigated conditions (4089 m3/ha total amount water). System boundary: an average year of the productive phase is regarded. Included are also the two non-productive years. Asparagus has a lifetime of 9 years and 7 years in the productive phase. The data are representative for asparagus production in China based on average data over the country.

Data quality rating (DQR) = 2.7 (i.e. good quality)

activityName: Cashew, in-shell, at farm (WFLDB)
comment:
This dataset represents the global average for cashew production for export, at farm. It is calculated as weighted average of the following countries, based on their respective export shares according to faostat data for 2012-2016, considering the cashew nuts kernels and the cashew nuts, in-shell exported amount (the cashew kenels correspond to 21% of the cashew in-shell weight according to http://hubrural.org/IMG/pdf/ci_cashew_analysis_06.pdf):
 - Ivory Coast: 14%
 - India: 15%
 - Vietnam: 32%
 
 
These countries together represent 61% of global export.
All farming activities documented in the respective national datasets are included. No transportation to the marketplace is considered.
The functional unit is the production of 1 kg of cashew nuts, in-shell, at farm.

Data quality rating (DQR) = 2.2, Good quality

Data source: 
faostat, export data, sum of cashew nuts kernels and cashew nuts in-shell, 2012-2016: http://www.fao.org/faostat/en/#data/TP
cashew kernel / cashew in-shell ratio: http://hubrural.org/IMG/pdf/ci_cashew_analysis_06.pdf

activityName: Chicken egg, poultry industrial laying systems, at farm (WFLDB)
comment:
The present dataset is built according to GLEAM 2.0 methodology (FAO 2018). It uses housing and feed storage data gathered by Agroscope for the WFLDB version 3.4 and found in the following datasets: 'Laying hen, in barn single tiered, at farm (WFLDB 3.4)/CN U' and 'Rearing hen, at farm (WFLDB 3.4)/CN U'. The two systems are merged and scaled to represent the chicken husbandry.

The full description of the animal production system is available in the WFLDB documentation report: Bengoa X., Chappuis C., Guignard C., Liernur A., Kounina A., Papadimitriou C., Rossi V. & Bayart J-B.  (2019) World Food LCA Database Documentation. Version 3.5, November 2019. Quantis, Lausanne, Switzerland.

Reference flow: The total weight of chicken eggs laid over one year in an industrial laying flock, at farm.

Included processes: The inventory includes the feed consumed by the total flock in one year, the laying and rearing hens husbandry systemsand feed transport from regional warehouse to animal farm, enteric emissions and manure management emissions. At the end of the egg producing round the laying hen is assumed to be burned in municipal incineration. Duration of egg laying is 406 days, with 310 eggs produced

Geography: Canada

Data quality rating (DQR) = 2.5   Good quality

Data sources:
- Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) (2018) Global Livestock Environmental Assessment Model, Model description Version 2.0.
- https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/t1/tbl1/en/tv.action?pid=3210011701 and https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/t1/tbl1/en/tv.action?pid=3210016601

activityName: Coconut, dehusked, at farm (WFLDB)
comment:
Included processes: The inventory includes the processes of irrigation, pesticide application, fertilisation and harvest. Machine use and infrastructure are excluded as most of the work is assumed to be manual work. Inputs of fertilisers, pesticides, irrigation and planted trees are included. Direct field emissions from crop production activities (e.g. fertiliser and pesticide use) and land use change are considered.

Remark: The functional unit is the production of 1 kg of coconut after manual dehusking at the farm. The co-product "Coconut husk, at farm" in included in the inventory.  The reference flow is the average yield per ha and year, from 2009 - 2012: yield (4.4 t/ha) obtained under irrigated conditions (total amount of water 3076 m3/ha). System boundary: an average year of the productive phase is regarded; included are also the per year of lifetime calculated emissions for nursery, materials for planting, establishment and clearing phase; at farm without storage. Number of years from planting to clearing (lifetime): 60 years. Tree density: 175 trees/ha.   - Waste treatment after clearing of the orchard: Wooden posts and tree wood go to incineration, concrete posts go to land fill, iron wires go to recycling. The data are representative for coconut production in Philippines used for the export market. Economic allocation between the coconut and the husk is considered, with allocation factors from the Agri-Footprint 1.0 "Economic allocation" database (i.e. 93% to the coconut, 7% to the husk).
Technology: Conventional production.

Comment: Statistical data from FAO used to assess land use change is incomplete for the Philippines. The original land use of 96.8 % of perennial cropland transformed in the last 20 years is unknown. To avoid a potentially significant underestimation of land use change impacts, the conservative assumption was made that the unknown land transformation share shall be attributed to transformation from forest land (primary and secondary).

Data quality rating (DQR) = 2.2 (i.e. good quality)

activityName: Mandarin, at farm (WFLDB)
comment:
Translated name: Mandarin, at farm (WFLDB 3.5)
Included processes: The inventory includes all activities of a year in the productive phase of the orchard, i.e. fertiliser and pesticide application, mulching, mowing, harvesting and irrigation. Machine infrastructure including a shed for shelter and fuel use are also considered as well as transport on the farm. Direct field emissions from crop production activities and from land use change are considered. The establishment phase of the orchard, i.e. tree nursery, soil cultivation, planting trees, sowing grass and irrigation. activityName: Raw cow milk archetype, feed mix IT-154, at farm (WFLDB)
comment:
Dairy farm archetype IT-154 according to FAO, IDF, IFCN (2014).
IT-154 represents an average-sized farm in northern Italy (Lombardy), having Holstein cows with a milk yield of 8 810 kg milk/cow per year. The cows are kept in a free stall barn where milking is done in a parlour system. The farm operates on 72 ha of land that is very fertile and can also be used for cash crops. About 56 percent of the work on the farm is done by family members.

Allocation between milk and meat (live animals) based on bio-physical causality (IDF 2015)
Inventory is for 1 kg raw milk, uncorrected. Mass produced is given for FPCM equivalent (IDF 2015)
Co-product is beef cattle, from dairy farm (culled cows and male calves).

Included: all feed inputs, pasture and pasture-related emissions, enteric emissions.
Excluded: milking, farm infrastructure and energy/water consumption, manure management, packaging, transport for raw milk collection.

Hence the raw milk archetypes datasets are intended to be used in the raw milk national mix datasets, where manure management, farm processes and local peat degradation are also combined. The inventory is presented for 1 kg uncorrected raw milk, but the output quantity is corrected to correspond to 1 kg of FPCM.

1 kg FPCM (fat and protein corrected milk)
1 kg LW (live weight) beef cattle, from dairy farm
Milk yield = 8810 kg year-1 cow-1
Number of dairy cows per farm = 154
Number of heifers per farm = 118 (avg)

Data quality rating (DQR) = 1.7 ( i.e. very good quality)

activityName: Sweet corn, at farm (WFLDB)
comment:
This dataset represents the global average for Sweet corn, at farm. It is calculated as weighted average of the following countries, based on their respective export shares according to FAOSTAT data for 2010:
 - Thailand: 25%
 - Hungary: 21%
 - United States: 17%
These countries together represent 63% of global export. 
All farming activities documented in the respective national datasets are included. No transportation to the marketplace is considered.
The functional unit is the production of 1 kg of Sweet corn.

Data quality rating (DQR) = 2.0 (i.e. very good quality)

activityName: Swine, industrial system, live weight, at farm (WFLDB)
comment:
The present dataset is built according to GLEAM 2.0 methodology (FAO 2018). It uses housing and feed storage data gathered by Agroscope for the WFLDB version 3.4 and found in the following datasets: 'Swine, live weight, at farm (WFLDB 3.4)/ES U' and 'Piglet, for fattening, at farm (WFLDB 3.4)/GLO U'. The two systems are merged and scaled to represent the overall beef live weight production.

The full description of the animal production system is available in the WFLDB documentation report: Bengoa X., Chappuis C., Guignard C., Liernur A., Kounina A., Papadimitriou C., Rossi V. & Bayart J-B.  (2019) World Food LCA Database Documentation. Version 3.5, November 2019. Quantis, Lausanne, Switzerland.

This archetype represents a 5000 heads industrial swine farm in North America, with 680 sows, 346 weaners, 3940 fattening pigs and 34 other pigs assimilated to sows in terms of housing.

Reference flow: The functional unit is the production of 1 kg of live weight swine at farm, ready for slaughtering. The reference flow is 1 year of swine farm that produces 2'103'898 kg live weight. The present model is based on the industrial swine production system described in the GLEAM report.

Allocation: No allocation

System boundaries:  Cradle-to-gate: The process includes the piglet for growing (25 kg/animal), the feed for the overall system (included for the piglet) and including its transport to the farm from the regional warehouse (assuming that all feed is purchased), the infrastructure on the farm, direct (enteric) emissions from animals to air and manure management emissions.  
The feed intake (DMI/year) for the overall industrial system as well as the total live wieght (LW) produced by the system are calculated based on the GLEAM model.

Average size of farm: 5000 heads
Managing system: industrial system

Data quality rating (DQR) = 2.3 (i.e good quality)

Geography: Canada

Technology: Average European technology

Time: 2009-2018

Data sources:
- Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) (2018) Global Livestock Environmental Assessment Model, Model description Version 2.0.

activityName: Tomato, fresh grade, open field, at farm (WFLDB)
comment:
Included processes: The inventory includes the processes of soil cultivation, planting, pesticide application, fertilisation and harvest. Machine infrastructure including a shed for shelter and fuel use are also considered as well as transport on farm. Inputs of fertilisers, pesticides, irrigation and seedlings are included. Direct field emissions from crop production activities (e.g. fertiliser and pesticide use) and land use change are considered.

Remark: The functional unit is the production of 1 kg of tomatoes for fresh consumption. The reference flow is the average yield per ha and year, from 2009 - 2012: yield (30.4 t/ha) obtained under irrigated conditions (total amount of water 4535 m3/ha).  The data are representative for fresh tomatoes for fresh consumption, produced in Mexico for the export market. 
Technology: Conventional production (open field).

Data quality rating (DQR) = 2.2 (i.e. good quality)

activityName: Vanilla, cured and dried beans, at farm (WFLDB)
comment:
Reference flow: The functional unit is the production of 1 kg cured and dried vanilla.

System Boundaries: Cradle-to-gate. This dataset covers the process of vanilla curing, including blanching, sweating, and drying of the green vanilla beans. The input green vanilla beans, as well as the energy and water use are included. Yield is 6.5 kg green beans per kg cured vanilla. Packaging is not included.

Geography: Madagascar

Technology: Traditional bleaching, sweating and sun-drying as practiced in Madagascar and India and described in the following websites, accessed December 2018.
http://www.varanashi.com/vanilla_processing.html
http://www.provagourmet.us/the-vanilla-process

It is assumed that water heated for 30-kg batches amounts to 90 L, with 5% loss for each batch (evaporation and extracted with the beans, dried). Water is completed regularly and thrown away after 10 batches in a row (10 times 5% loss). So 90 L are used and returned to surface water, and 45 L are used in addition and evaporated / evacuated with the blanched beans and dried. Total 135 L for 300 kg dried beans.
Water is heated with firewood from 20°C to 65°C, assuming 40% energy loss each batch (in addition to energy loss via water loss) because of the heat needed to heat the beans (0.33 kg/L, assuming similar heat capacity to water) and other losses. Firewood related LUC is ignored at this stage. The situation in Madagascar is critical in this regard, but firewood can be sourced from plantations planted on degraded land being restored, so refinement is needed.

The use of clean blankets is critical for the success of the sweating process. The cleaning is done in hot water with similar assumptions as above, plus the following: One blanket is used for each 30-kg batch (which becomes lighter while drying, obviously). Cleaning 1 blanket requires about 5 L of water at 70°C. 10% of that water is evaporated.

Shade drying is done in a room filled with wooden boxes (with 1 batch in each) and artificially ventilated 24x7 during 2 to 3 months. Assumptions are made on the number of boxes and the power of the ventilation system.

Time: Data from 2010 - 2018

Data quality rating (DQR) = 2.7, Good quality

activityName: Walnut, in shell, dried, at farm (WFLDB)
comment:
Reference flow: The functional unit is the production of 1 kg of walnut, in shell, dried, at the farm (in practice, dehusking and drying generally take place in a separate facility). 6.72 t/ha, obtained under irrigated conditions (total  amount of water 10660 m3/ha). According to Yilmaz 2017, the total fresh walnut, with its green husk is 2.65 times the in-shell dried walnut.

Allocation: No allocation

System boundaries: Cradle-to-gate. The inventory includes the processes of seedling production and planting, fertilizer and pesticide application, irrigation and harvest. Equipment infrastructure is also considered, such as for sprinkler irrigation. Direct field emissions from crop production activities (fertiliser and pesticide use) and land use change (LUC) are considered. The processing of dehusking and drying is also included, even if occuring at plant and not directly at farm, to obtain in-shell dried walnuts. Number of years from planting to clearing (lifetime): 25 years. 

Data quality rating (DQR) = 1.2, Excellent quality

Geography: USA

Technology: Conventional production

Time: 2016-2017

Data sources: 
- Grant 2017: Grant J A, Caprile J L, Doll, D A, Murdock J, 2017. Sample costs to establish an orchard and produce walnuts, San Joaquin Valley - North, Late leafing - lateral bearing. UC Davis Department of agricultural and resources economics report. Downloaded on https://coststudyfiles.ucdavis.edu/uploads/cs_public/1d/05/1d05d59d-706e-4937-8e05-5563b7468e23/2017-walnutssjvn-final_draft.pdf, August 2019.
- Yilmaz 2017: Yilmaz S, Akça Y, Saçlik S, 2017. Green husk and Inshell biomass production capabilities of six walnut cultivars. J Internation Scientific Publications, Agriculture & Food. Vol 5. 
- Various websites consulted for the concentration in active ingredients of the pesticides, detailed for each pesticide flow on input/output tab.
